data.long_meaning: Aradhy is a Sanskrit name that is derived from the word ‘aradhana’, which means ‘worship’. This name is given to a child who is believed to be worthy of adoration and reverence. The name Aradhy carries the meaning “Worshipped, Adored” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Aradhy usually hope their child will grow to embody worshipped, adored and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Aradhya is a form of the goddess Parvati, also known as Shukla-Saraswati. She is particularly revered in the Tantra tradition of Hinduism. The word 'Aradhy' means 'worth-worshipping'.

Another reference to Aradhya is found in the Mahabharata, where she is mentioned as the goddess who is worshipped by the sage Vyasa during the composition of the epic. This is believed to have taken place during the Kurukshetra war around 800 BC.
